doc_screened_files.reason: Most directly matches the failure: the query trace hits `object_safety_violations` / `is_object_safe`, and this file owns object-safety checks for traits and associated items. The bug is about method signatures on trait objects admitting an associated type from the wrong supertrait substitution, so the object-safety checker is the most likely root cause.

This file enforces object-safety and trait-object formation while lowering `dyn` types, including validation of associated type bounds and `Self`-dependent rules. If the bad substitution is accepted during trait-object lowering, the unsound `dyn Foo<T, U>` construction in the reproducer can slip through here.

Its responsibility explicitly includes constructing the normalized supertrait and item-bound obligations for object-type candidates. The issue text says we should "deeply normalize these supertraits" and compare associated-type substitutions modulo regions, which aligns closely with this candidate-assembly layer.

Object safety ultimately feeds vtable construction and method dispatch, and this module computes trait-object vtable structure and supertrait slots. If a method signature is treated as object-safe when it should not be, the vtable-layer consequences would show up here next.

The trace includes `predicates_of`, `explicit_item_super_predicates`, and `trait_explicit_predicates_and_bounds`, all of which point at predicate collection for traits and supertraits. If associated-type substitutions from supertraits are being lost before object-safety checking, this collector is a plausible source.

This file builds explicit and elaborated item bounds, including inherited bounds from enclosing traits. Since the bug hinges on supertrait-associated type substitutions and their bounds, bad bound propagation here could cause the object-safety check to see the wrong projection shape.

The trait-object vtable data model includes supertrait vtables and method entries. If object-safety lets an invalid associated-type projection through, the downstream trait-object representation here can reflect the same incorrect assumption.

Well-formedness generates obligations for trait refs and object predicates. Because the reproducer relies on a `where <Self as Mirror>::Assoc: Super<...>` constraint and supertrait relationships, a missed or weakened WF obligation could help the bad object-safety result survive.

Associated-item metadata and lookup live here. The bug is specifically about associated types in method signatures, so any mismatch between the associated item being referenced and the substituted supertrait projection could originate in associated-item bookkeeping.

This module owns trait-definition metadata and impl indexing, which underpin supertrait and associated-item lookup during object-safety and vtable reasoning. It is less likely than the higher-level object-safety code, but still part of the path that resolves which supertraits and associated items apply.
